name: Petrol and diesel
summary: Petrol (gasoline), diesel and kerosene for engines, generators, heaters and lamps. The vapour explodes: no flames, sparks or phones nearby, and never siphon by mouth.
uses: Running generators, vehicles and small engines

Diesel and kerosene for heaters and lamps. Keep lamp oil and other liquid fuels out of young children's reach or locked away: swallowed or inhaled, they can reach the lungs with severe effects, even death (Health Canada oil lamps). See the guide Keep lamp oil and torch fuel away from children
Petrol for chainsaws and garden tools
identify: Underground tanks at fuel stations (need a hand pump), vehicle tanks, farm diesel tanks, generator day tanks at hospitals, phone sites and data centres, boat tanks, and cans in garages and sheds. Diesel is oily and yellowish (farm and off-road diesel is often dyed red); petrol is thin and sharp-smelling.
test: Look in a clear jar: Water settles at the bottom as beads or a layer; sludge or separate layers mean leave it. Date every can when you fill it (Alberta farm fuel).

decay.note: Estimate. Alberta's farm-fuel guide says use petrol within a month of buying, 6 months at best, and diesel within 6–12 months; heater kerosene no more than 6 months (Toyotomi KS-27A).
